result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers map plans to the three groups, and their margin arithmetic checks out. Each has small internal contradictions: A says its search caps equal its usage guesses but doesn't follow that, and B places RAW support both on every tier and as a Pro addition. B edges ahead because its +1 TB add-on fills the 1–5 TB gap and its caveats cover app-store fees and over-quota behavior. A gets credit for higher margins and a clear 'would change if' section. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers have correct margin arithmetic, place features sensibly, cap AI search per tier, and present their prices as assumptions to check against beta data. A covers the 1–5 TB photographer range more smoothly with a $19.99 add-on per extra TB, while B jumps from $29 for 1 TB straight to $119 for 5 TB. B's 300 GB Family cap only just covers the stated range. B also has small flaws: its assumed casual search volume (100) doesn't match its stated cap (200), and it ends with a stray handoff line.
